result.title: When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners
result.summary: When a recurrent reasoner returns a wrong answer, is its computation finished or merely stopped? We test this on a trained Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM; 27M parameters, Sudoku-Extreme) by running the recurrence for one more inference budget and comparing with an unperturbed control. Solved answers persist (0.95 of 512 endpoints). Wrong answers mostly do not: 0.42 of near-miss answers (n=170) and 0.18 of all 512 wrong endpoints keep their answer. Perturbations from 0.05x to 20x the terminal-update scale barely change these rates, so the measurement reflects continued recurrence, not noise sensitivity. The solved-above-wrong ordering also holds in five further settings (a second seed, TRM, Maze, GRAM-guided TRM, N-Queens), but a fixed 1/2 persistence threshold does not, and neither do HRM's endpoint-spectrum and fast-versus-slow predictability patterns, which are not universal diagnostics. Perturb-and-reselect (known from prior work) is consistent with this: frozen noise gains 4.8 accuracy points (197 gained, 2 lost), but compute-matched extended depth gains 5.6 and Sudoku symmetry augmentation 34.6, so noise is not the best use of the budget. Conclusions are limited to finite horizons and one primary HRM checkpoint; they do not exclude asymptotic attractors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 27M 参数的 HRM（Sudoku-Extreme）上延长递归推理预算，比较正确答案与错误答案的持续性，并在多种设置中检验端点谱、快慢预测模式及不同预算使用方式的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断循环式 latent reasoner 返回答案时计算是否真正收敛，对 THINK/STOP 的收益成本、错误状态延续和停止判据研究具有直接参考价值，值得优先阅读。
